newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cabinet to decide on telecom sale next week.
newsitem.headline: Polish cabinet to decide on telecom sale next week.

text.p: Poland's government will discuss the method of privatising the country's telecom monopoly TPSA next week, but the sell-off will probably not come this year, Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz said.
"We will debate concepts of privatising TPSA next week...But the privatisation is unlikely to be started this year," Cimoszewicz told Reuters in a Thursday interview.

He said the cabinet would decide on how quickly TPSA should be sold, how big a stake should be retained by the treasury and whether to offer shares to a strategic investor or only float some of its shares on bourses.
He said Poland should not privatise TPSA too hastily so as to wait for the best moment on the international equity markets, when the sale would generate most revenues.

"A speedy privatisation might prove financially unprofitable. The sale needs to be inscribed in the scenarios of similar privatisations in other countries so that our offer does not compete with others," he said.
He confirmed that some of TPSA's shares would be earmarked to help finance the coming reform of the social security system.
Under a tentative plan, the government is to issue bonds convertible into shares of privatised companies to finance the creation of new pension funds.
